**STEP 1 - Scene:** Two small cucumber maki (rolls) on a white plate, photographed from above. The plate is on a dark striped tablecloth.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate looks like a side plate, about 20 cm in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 10² = 314 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** (1) sushi rice, (2) nori seaweed wrapper, (3) cucumber strips. No sauce or oil is visible.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The two rolls together cover about 4% of the plate (about 13 cm²), so the food covers only a small share of the plate.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Each roll is about 2.7 cm in diameter and about 2.3 cm long, so each is roughly 13 ml. Two pieces give about 26 ml gross.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Sushi rice is compact, so I use a density of about 0.9 g/ml, giving about 23 g. Splitting this by component: rice about 18 g, nori about 2 g, cucumber about 2 g. Total about 22 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Seasoned sushi rice is about 150 kcal/100 g, so 18 g gives about 27 kcal. Nori is about 35 kcal/100 g, so 2 g gives about 7 kcal. Cucumber is about 15 kcal/100 g, so 2 g gives about 0.3 kcal. Total about 34 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two small maki pieces at about 22 g and about 34 kcal is plausible. A single maki piece is typically about 15–25 g, and this is a small portion on a large plate.
